text: Three authors  - Andrea Bartz, Charles Graeber, and Kirk Wallace Johnson - sued Anthropic, alleging their flagship AI model Claude was trained on millions of pirated e-books downloaded from 'shadow libraries' like LibGen without permission. The case set major legal precedents for generative AI training and fair use, ruling specifically that the use of 'pirated copies' of books for training is not fair use. In August 2025, Anthropic settled the case for $1.5 billion to compensate rights holders - the largest copyright settlement in US history. Currently there are delays over excessive lawyers fees ($320m!) and issues around whether Anthropic agrees to restrict the future use of pirated works.
